To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have determined the crystallographic structure of the human chemokine thymus and activating-regulated chemokines (TARC) at 1.9 angstroms resolution.
we have crystallized TARC and have determined the unit-cell parameters for three crystal forms, and that we have collected diffraction data for one of the crystal forms to 1.8 A resolution.
we have determined the three-dimensional structure of TARC at a resolution of 1.85 Å.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of a CC chemokines, TARC.
the structure determination of the TARC chemokine.
the structure of the chemokines and the receptors that they bind to.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TARC crystals diffract to high resolution, and the triclinics are the best for structure solution.
the three crystal forms represent different crystal packing of the same molecule.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the three different crystal forms of TARC are all suitable for X-ray structure determination and that the triclinics crystals are the best of the three forms.
we have obtained three different crystals that are suitable for structure solution.
TARC crystallized in three different forms, which are all amenable to X-ray crystallographic analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to obtain good-quality crystals of a chemokine, even one with a relatively low molecular weight.
TARC can be produced in milligram quantities and that it crystallizes well in a number of different crystal forms.
it is feasible to crystallize a chemokine, even one that is difficult to express, and that the crystals diffract to a high resolution.
